narrative.summary: The Central African Republic has no published AI-specific law, strategy or guidance. Its only AI-relevant national instrument is the 2024 personal data protection law (Law 24.001), which defines profiling and gives people the right to know and contest the logic of automated decisions with legal effects. A national AI strategy for 2024-2028 has been mentioned by a minister but not published, and no official text has been identified for a 2024 cybersecurity law or for an announced AI centre of excellence.

instruments.english_title: Law No. 24.001 on the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly (adopted) and President of the Republic (promulgated)
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 25 January 2024; Art. 58 states it takes effect from its promulgation and is to be published in the Journal officiel. Not yet verified from the official text: the Journal officiel reference. Art. 57 gave the ministry in charge of the digital economy, posts and telecommunications 12 months to set up the data protection agency, with the ministry exercising its functions in the meantime. Not yet verified from the official text: establishment of the agency. Copy published on the website of the telecom regulator ARCEP-RCA.
instruments.summary: The Central African Republic's first general personal data protection law, applying to processing by controllers or processors established in the country and to processing that produces effects there, including public security and defence subject to specific derogations. It sets core processing principles, cross-border transfer rules, prior declaration/authorisation formalities, data subject rights and sanctions, and places compliance under an independent administrative data protection agency. It defines profiling and, under Art. 30, gives individuals a right to information allowing them to know and contest the logic of automated processing where a decision based on it produces legal effects on them.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law governing personal data used in AI training and use; includes a profiling definition and a right to know and contest the logic of automated decisions (Art. 30).
